name: Authorization Checklist
description: This module is a pre-completion checklist for authorization work: a short set of checks to run before calling a authorization task done.
content:
This module is a pre-completion checklist for authorization work: a short set of checks to run before calling a authorization task done.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When multiple authorization strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
2. Prefer the simplest authorization approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
3. Surface known limitations of a chosen authorization approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
4. Keep authorization changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
5. State assumptions about authorization explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
6. Measure before optimizing any authorization bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
7. When authorization decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
8. Document any non-obvious authorization decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
9. Keep authorization outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic authorization advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of authorization correctness.
- Avoid mixing unrelated authorization concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not silently drop authorization edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not skip documenting authorization assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for authorization, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
